_comment: The source of truth for koinosai.com/updates and for the What's new link in the app's update popup. Newest first. Every kaiapp [release] MUST add an entry here in the same session it ships, or a tester gets a popup pointing at a version the page has never heard of. `kind` is one of: new, fix, change.

releases.title: Your password guards where returns go

changes.text: Arming automatic returns to another address now asks for your wallet password. The rule everywhere else in the app is that anything moving value to an address you do not control proves the password on that call — a one-off send obeyed it, arming a repeating one did not, even though it keeps moving value on its own for as long as it stays armed. Your wallet unlocks itself at start-up, so “unlocked” was never evidence that you were at the keyboard. Percentage, minimum, cap, interval, pausing and compounding back into your own VHP still ask for nothing, because none of them can move a satoshi anywhere your wallet does not already own.

Your node now proves it owns the wallet it earns as. Registering with the network was taken on trust, so anyone who could reach the scheduler could register under someone else's address and collect their jobs and their place on the payout roster. Your node signs the claim with the same key it already signs every receipt with. Nothing changes for you: nodes on older builds keep working while everyone updates, and a machine that cannot sign still earns and tells you why rather than dropping off the network.

The three Koinos models now say what they actually are. Koinos Fast, Balanced and Smart described what they were for and nothing else, so there was no way to find out they run Qwen 2.5 1.5B, Llama 3.2 3B and Qwen 2.5 7B — which is the first thing worth knowing when you are deciding what to download, or comparing against a hosted API. Every other card in the catalog already named its model.
Email dependencies updated to clear a batch of security advisories in the mail-parsing chain. No change to how mail works.

releases.title: The X button, and three holes a reviewer found

changes.text: Closing the window no longer closes the app. Koinos AI tucks itself down by the clock and keeps running, so your node stays connected and keeps earning — click the tray icon to bring the window back, or right-click it and choose Quit to stop for real. The first time it happens the app tells you where it went and offers to go back to closing outright; Settings › Closing the window flips it either way.

Your local API no longer answers other websites. It is open to programs on your machine on purpose, and until you created an API key that included a page in another browser tab — which could start a request you never saw, on your hardware and, off Local-Only, your KAI. Programs on this machine are unaffected.

Koinos Code can no longer be walked out of a project folder by a symlink committed into a repository. It clones repositories, so this was reachable by asking it to work on one; the project boundary is now checked against the real filesystem rather than by comparing paths as text.

Web pages the AI fetches are checked by where they actually lead, not how the address is spelled. A domain pointing at your own machine, or a public page redirecting to one, is refused — including at every redirect along the way.
Qwen 2.5 14B no longer describes itself as the biggest model in the list. It stopped being that several releases ago.

releases.title: The switch you couldn't see

changes.text: The new Remote access switch in v0.50.0 was invisible — the button was there, its visual toggle wasn't. It now looks like every other switch in the app. Reported within the hour; thanks.

releases.title: Your API, from anywhere

changes.text: Remote access: one switch in the Local API view gives your API a public address that works from anywhere — a phone, a server, another computer. No router setup, nothing to install: the app keeps an outbound connection to koinosai.com and answers through it. Your API key still decides who gets in, and the switch refuses to turn on until you have one, so your API is never left open.

The address is stable and private to your app — it stays the same across restarts, and nobody can claim it. Turn the switch off and it goes dead immediately. Only the API crosses; the app's tools and files never leave your machine.

The Koinos Node dashboard sometimes flashed zeros — 0 mana, a $0.00 node value — and then recovered on its own. That was the public Koinos RPC having a slow moment, and the app treating "couldn't read it" as "it's zero". It now holds the last real numbers and marks them as catching up instead of scaring you with zeros.
Plain honesty about remote access: traffic to your public address passes through koinosai.com on its way to your computer. The switch's own description says the same.

releases.title: Earning gets out of your way

changes.text: A tester's PC froze when Earn ran alongside heavy GPU design work, and recovered the instant the app closed. Cause found: the AI engine kept the model's weights loaded in GPU memory the whole time earning was on, and when another program needed that memory, Windows ground to a halt shuffling it. Thanks for the precise report — "closing the app fixes it" was the clue that cracked it.

Earning now watches your GPU. When your other programs are really using it, earning pauses, releases all of its GPU memory immediately, and steps off the network roster. After about two minutes of quiet it comes back on its own. You never have to manage this.
The Earn screen says when this happens — an amber "Paused — your computer is busy with other work" instead of a worker that looks broken.
The AI engine now runs at below-normal priority, so when your work and earning both want the processor, your work wins.

The pause is automatic only on NVIDIA graphics cards for now (the ones the app uses for GPU serving). Dedicated earning rigs that never share the machine can switch it off with the earn.courtesy setting.

releases.title: Every update tells you what is in it

changes.text: This page. Every release, what changed in it, and why — at koinosai.com/updates.

The update popup now has a What's new button that opens the notes for the exact version being offered, so you can read what you are installing before you restart. Reading them does not count as declining the update — it stays queued.
Settings shows a What's new link next to the version you are running.

releases.title: Your node tells you when its stake is sitting idle

changes.text: The app now compares the VHP your block producer says it is using against the VHP your wallet actually holds. A field machine was producing with 41% of its stake — running, in sync, making blocks, and quietly leaving most of its VHP out of the lottery. Nothing on any screen said so, because every number was individually correct.
When the two disagree, the Earn tab and your dashboard both say so, say what it is costing, and tell you to restart the Koinos node so the producer re-reads your stake.

The check is one-directional and tolerates 2%: VHP is consumed as blocks are produced, so the log figure trails the balance slightly, and a false alarm telling you to restart a node is worse than silence.

releases.title: The dashboard can tell an old app from a quiet chain

changes.text: The app reports its own version with each node snapshot, so koinosai.com/dashboard can say whether a missing figure means the app is out of date or the chain simply did not answer this time. Two identical-looking blanks with opposite fixes.
The Earn tab's block-producer row now points at your dashboard, which is where those figures moved.

releases.title: The whole node picture on the web, kept fresh

changes.text: koinosai.com/dashboard — your machines in one place, with AI and Koinos split into their own sections. Node value, estimated daily, weekly and yearly earnings, KOIN, VHP, share of the network and expected block rate.
Links both ways: the account page points at the dashboard, and the dashboard has Chat and Account in its nav.
Your machine now refreshes its node figures every 5 minutes instead of only when it reconnects, which could be hours. The account page was showing a genuinely stale copy.
The account page is an account page again — sign-in methods and linked wallets, with the node detail moved to the dashboard.

releases.title: Say why the block-producer card is missing

changes.text: An absent producer card had several possible causes and none were visible. The Earn tab now names the reason: node stopped, log unreadable, or Earning switched off — the report travels with the worker connection, so there is no report without it.

releases.title: Fix the crash behind USDT node funding

changes.text: Typing an amount into Fund node with USDT threw "Cannot find module './lib/usdt-send'". A lazy require pointed at the wrong path in packaged builds.
A test now scans every relative require in the packaged source, so a path that only breaks after packaging cannot ship again.

releases.title: Your block producer, reported alongside the AI worker

changes.text: The app reads its own block_producer log and reports your producing VHP, your share of the network, and how often you should expect a block. Small producers go quiet for hours perfectly normally, so the app puts a probability on the silence rather than implying a fault.

releases.title: Show the market price, not a buy quote

changes.text: KOIN was reading about 1.9% high. A quote taken from a pool includes the 1% fee and the price impact of the trade size — that is what you would pay, not what the market says. Both are now removed, which brings it within 0.06% of what other venues show.

releases.title: Node value and estimated earnings in dollars

changes.text: A Node value box on the Koinos dashboard, plus estimated daily, weekly and yearly earnings in USD, priced off the Uniswap vKOIN/USDT pool.
Earnings estimates say "not enough history yet" until there is measured history, rather than printing $0.00 at you.

releases.title: A source install can tell you it is behind

changes.text: Installed from a git checkout there is no update feed and no installer, so nothing ever mentioned a new version. The app now checks git, offers to fast-forward and restart itself, and when it cannot, says exactly why and prints the commands that finish the job.

releases.title: The arm64 build the Raspberry Pi was waiting for

changes.text: On arm64 the updater asks for latest-linux-arm64.yml. No arm64 build was publishing one, so every check quietly 404'd into an empty catch. There is now an arm64 AppImage, and failed checks are logged instead of discarded.

releases.title: A task that is running looks like it is running

changes.text: Pressing Run now appeared to do nothing. The feedback was being wiped by the list's own 5-second repaint before anyone could see it.

releases.title: Scheduled tasks stop asking for a key they never needed

changes.text: A scheduled task failed with "Missing or invalid API key" as soon as you created any API key of your own. Tasks were going out through the public API instead of the local path.

releases.title: Removing a model no longer freezes the window

changes.text: Uninstalling a large model froze the entire app — no typing, no clicking, dropdowns dead. The delete was synchronous and running on the thread that routes every keystroke and draws every menu. Deleting 4.7 GB stopped the window for as long as it took.

releases.title: The remove buttons are visible again

changes.text: The uninstall × on a model was invisible until hovered, and it was shoving the Use button into the middle of the row. The same invisible-until-hover bug was also hiding the delete control on scheduled tasks.

releases.title: Choose where the node keeps its data, and remove models you are done with

changes.text: Pick the Koinos node's data folder at setup or move it later, with a safe move that verifies before it deletes anything.
Uninstall installed models to free disk.
